clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within the following year: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to your mother's house every evening; your father took night shifts and distanced from your mother; your uncle Anton's drinking worsened and he separated from Celeste; your mother's anxiety rose over Anton; your brother Callum developed ear infections through the winter. These shifts pile up in the months after the death, each person reacting near another's.

clusters.name: Odette's bed rest in pregnancy, 1984–1984
clusters.reason: Around your mother's bed rest ordered in March 1984: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep house, then argued with your father over how she kept it; your brother Callum stammered again after a year free of it. Three shifts pile up within a few months as your mother's functioning fell and your grandmother stepped in, with conflict between them and your brother reacting alongside.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis in September 1986, over the following decade: your grandfather Ambrose took over her cooking and appointments, then her care deepened as she fell and lost function; your father's anxiety rose and he phoned his father nightly for news; he and Lyle argued over who should help their parents, then Lyle distanced; your father's drinking worsened; your aunt Pearl developed panic spells; and through these years your grandmother's function fell, rose briefly, then fell again until she moved to the nursing home in 1997. Shifts pile up over years with no settling between them, each step a deepening of the family's reactive moves around her decline.

clusters.name: Callum's leaving for work up north, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum's departure for a mining job up north in May 1999: your father and Callum argued over his plans before he left; your mother's anxiety rose at the thought of him so far away; your father's functioning fell and he sat late in the garage; your sister Ines skipped school through the autumn; your mother began taking Ines everywhere with her. By August 2000, Ines returned to school and passed her exams. The shifts pile up around Callum's leaving, with your parents and sister each reacting in the months after, and settle as Ines's attendance steadied.

clusters.name: Hazel's death, 2003–2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's death in January 2003: within months your sleep fell to a few hours a night, your functioning at work fell and you were let go in May, you dreaded crowds and went out only after dark, and your anxiety rose. These shifts in you alone pile up through the spring and summer, with no one else's shifts shown in those months, and settle by November when you took a job at the garden centre and slept through the night again.
